ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An object moving in uniform circular motion travels $100\mathrm{m}$ along a circle with a radius of $20\mathrm{m}$ in $10\mathrm{s}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the linear velocity?
2. What is the magnitude of the angular velocity?
3. What is the magnitude of centripetal acceleration?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An object moving in uniform circular motion travels $100\mathrm{m}$ along a circle with a radius of $20\mathrm{m}$ in $10\mathrm{s}$. 1. What is the magnitude of the linear velocity? 2. What is the magnitude of the angular velocity? 3. What is the magnitude of centripetal acceleration?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From the text, the object travels an arc length s = 100 m on a circle of radius r = 20 m in time t = 10 s. The magnitude of linear velocity is v = s/t = 100 m / 10 s = 10 m/s. The angular velocity is omega = v/r = (10 m/s)/(20 m) = 0.5 rad/s. The centripetal acceleration is a_c = v^2/r = (10 m/s)^2 / 20 m = 100/20 m/s^2 = 5 m/s^2.
